figures.claim: Its tibial attachment is between Gerdy's tubercle and the head of the fibula, about 5 to 10 mm below the joint line.
It was described by Segond in 1879 as a pearly resistant band, named and renamed many times since, and described again in 2013 in the paper that brought it back into use.
It was described by Segond in 1879 as a pearly resistant band, named and renamed many times since, and described again in 2013 in the paper that brought it back into use.
Conventional teaching places its centre about mid way between Gerdy's tubercle and the fibular head, about 7 mm below the joint line.
Conventional teaching gives the ligament a length of the order of 35 mm and a thickness of a few millimetres, which makes it thin relative to its length.
It restrains internal rotation, with its contribution rising between about 30 and 90 degrees of flexion.
